title: Python: a loop, while or with body that assigns __all__ is certified as an unconditional __all__ by starSetIsExact
description: GCLI-120 round 2 finding F3, measured. s.py is 'for _ in []:' with '__all__ = ["helper"]' in its body, then 'def helper(): pass' and 'for len in [1]: pass'; app.py is 'from s import *' with 'len(x)' in a function. The __all__ binding is not marked conditional (loop, while and with bodies count as unconditional in isConditionalStatement, calls.ts ~1792; maySkipStatement ~1840 knows they may be skipped), so starSetIsExact certifies the set and len(x) is claimed as the unshadowed builtin (resolvedExternal 1); in Python __all__ is never assigned when the loop does not run, so the star binds len. Measured on dev cbf219c and on e1dc2fc: the same claim, so it predates GCLI-120 and is the part of N1 that #210 did not fix. The while and with forms measure the same. Control (no __all__): nameNotBound 1 on e1dc2fc, resolvedExternal 1 on cbf219c. Joins the (a49) item 7 hold list beside GCLI-122.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a __all__ assigned in a for, while or with body is not certified exact: len(x) is not claimed as the builtin, red before and green after, one fixture per body form
a positive twin with an unconditional __all__ still certifies
a mutant that restores the isConditionalStatement reading is observed red

finalSummary: Landed as opum-ai/glyph-cli#214 (squash 3b9662d) after Opus round 1 BLOCK at 0551322 (chained x = __all__ = v lost its claim) and round 2 APPROVE at d9082791. An __all__ plain assignment in a statement that maySkipStatement says may be skipped (for/while body or else, with body, case, if arm, except arm, try body with an except) no longer makes a star's export set exact (new RawBinding.maySkip, set from the enclosing simple statement, read only by starSetIsExact), so the star is partial and a name it might bind (a for target len) is not claimed as the builtin; unconditional, try-only-finally, finally and chained module-level __all__ keep the claim. Verified by fixtures run against dev and the fix (six body forms red on dev and green after, guards for if/except forms, twins), mutants M-maySkip, M-stmt and M-chain observed red, and the five-pin corpus output byte-identical to dev (sha256 4839ad00c598e09909a8ed7f6f3f2450ef91502b8cde22d71c5ea0bbbba7c9ce). Per DEC-303 (a69) the fixtures pin the outcome and the nameNotBound bin only; the reason glyph-cli measures is 'unbound', not 'star-bound', which is filed separately.
